solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Book magazine for mature audience runs out of merchandise (3,4,7)

indicatorNotes.out of: OLDIE and R come out of, i.e. follow, the merchandise

blocks.note: The Oldie, a British magazine aimed at older readers
R = runs, the cricket scorecard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A publisher's catalogue: a magazine for older readers has sold out of its stock.
annotation.walkthrough: The Oldie is a British humour and lifestyle magazine for older readers. The answer is Ford Madox Ford's 1915 novel.
annotation.definitionFit: The Good Soldier is a novel by Ford Madox Ford, so it is a book.

entries.clue: Eccentric president introduces advantageous measure (5,4)

indicatorNotes.introduces: the president comes first and introduces the eccentric

blocks.note: a card = an eccentric or comic person

annotation.surface: An odd head of state brings in a policy that benefits someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' reads as an adjective describing the president, but it is a noun, CARD, placed after him.
annotation.definitionFit: A trump card is a resource or move that gives you the advantage.

entries.clue: One demanding money from former company employee (7)

blocks.note: an actor is employed by a theatre company

annotation.surface: Someone extorting cash from a man who used to work at the firm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Company' suggests a business, but here it is a theatre company, whose employee is an actor.
annotation.definitionFit: An exactor is one who exacts, i.e. demands payment.

entries.clue: Religious group summons state of harmony (5)

blocks.note: a monastic community, such as the Benedictines
a summons is a command to appear

annotation.surface: A sect calls its members to a state of peace.
annotation.walkthrough: In fact three definitions: 'summons' reads as the verb in the sentence, but it is a noun, an order.
annotation.definitionFit: Order means a religious community, and also calm, harmonious arrangement.

entries.clue: Diligent editor in charge of obsolete presses (9)

indicatorNotes.presses: the obsolete word presses the others inside it

blocks.note: dated = obsolete, split D…ATED around the rest

annotation.surface: A hard-working editor running outdated printing presses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Presses' looks like printing machinery to suit the editor, but it is a verb: DATED squeezes ED and IC.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone dedicated to their work gives it steady, careful effort.

entries.clue: Former blonde wanting bleach primarily for new style (5)

indicatorNotes.primarily: 'primarily' means in the first place, so only the first letter of bleach is taken
indicatorNotes.for new style: the remaining letters are given a new arrangement

blocks.note: BLONDE without B, the first letter of bleach

annotation.surface: A woman who used to be blonde stops bleaching her hair and tries a new look.
annotation.walkthrough: The hairdressing surface hides a simple deletion then rearrangement.
annotation.definitionFit: Olden means of former times, as in 'the olden days'.

entries.clue: Notice society girl in The Face (9)

indicatorNotes.in: society and girl go inside the face

blocks.note: dial = face, slang (and a clock face); split DI…AL

annotation.surface: An instruction to spot a debutante featured in The Face, a fashion magazine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Notice' reads as a verb, but the definition is the noun, as in being given your notice. The Face was a British style magazine; dial is slang for face.
annotation.definitionFit: Being given notice means being dismissed from a job.

entries.clue: Great rapper failing to hold last note regularly (7)

indicatorNotes.failing to hold last: the rapper's name loses its last letter

blocks.note: N and T, the 1st and 3rd letters of NOTE

annotation.surface: A star rapper can't sustain the final note of a song.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great' looks like praise for the rapper, but it is the definition. Holding a note is singing; here it just means keeping a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of distinguished: great and eminent figures are both ones who stand out.

entries.clue: Faculty originally translated nunc est bibendum the wrong way (4)

indicatorNotes.originally: take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of translated, nunc, est, bibendum

annotation.surface: A university department mistranslates Horace's Latin 'now is the time for drinking'.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Faculty' suggests a university department, but here it means a natural talent. Nunc est bibendum is from Horace: 'now we must drink'.
annotation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural aptitude, a faculty for something.

entries.clue: University backed faculty boss checking papers without staff? (7)

indicatorNotes.backed: the faculty boss is written backwards
indicatorNotes.checking: the reversed word holds (checks, restrains) the papers

blocks.note: the dean heads a faculty; reversed to NAED and split NA…ED

annotation.surface: A university dean inspects paperwork with no staff to help.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: without staff means without help, not only without employees.
annotation.definitionFit: Unaided means without help, as if without assistants or a supporting stick.

entries.clue: Intend secret to be kept from family (7)

indicatorNotes.to be kept from: the family is kept away from, i.e. removed from, the secret

blocks.note: clan = family, removed from the front

annotation.surface: A secret that must not be told to the relatives.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a family secret; the family, CLAN, sits literally inside the word for secret.
annotation.definitionFit: To destine is to intend or set apart for a purpose.

entries.clue: Safe seat finally accepted by member of House of Lords (5)

indicatorNotes.finally: 'finally' means at the end, so only the last letter of seat is taken
indicatorNotes.accepted by: the peer takes the letter in

blocks.note: a peer sits in the House of Lords; split PE…ER

annotation.surface: A secure constituency is taken over by a lord.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Safe seat' is a single political phrase, but it splits: Safe is the definition. Peter is old criminal slang for a safe.
annotation.definitionFit: In underworld slang a peter is a safe, hence a safe-cracker is a peterman.

entries.clue: Bold study reflected uncertainty and evidence of impact (9)

indicatorNotes.reflected: the word for uncertainty is mirrored

blocks.note: an if = a doubt; reflected to FI
a dent shows where something hit

annotation.surface: A daring piece of research shows doubt and the marks left by a collision.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reflected' reads as 'showed' with study, but it works on the word after it, reversing IF.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a bold manner and a confident one both show no fear of failing.

entries.clue: Mad race around island involves flying boat performing stunts (9)

indicatorNotes.Mad: something mad is disordered, so the letters of race lose their order
indicatorNotes.around: the scrambled race goes round the island
indicatorNotes.involves: that group takes in the boat
indicatorNotes.flying: letters sent flying scatter and land in a new order

annotation.surface: A frantic contest round an island features a seaplane doing tricks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flying boat' is a real aircraft that fits the stunt picture, but 'flying' is an anagram indicator on 'boat'.
annotation.definitionFit: Aerobatics are loops, rolls and dives flown for display, so an aerobatic pilot is one performing stunts.

entries.clue: Associate academic finishes teaching course (9)

indicatorNotes.finishes: the academic finishes, i.e. comes at the end of, the teaching course

annotation.surface: A junior lecturer completes a teacher-training course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Associate academic' looks like a job title; Associate is the definition, and BEd is the British teaching degree.
annotation.definitionFit: A bedfellow is an associate or ally, as in 'strange bedfellows'.

entries.clue: Firm sanctioned about member involved in dodgy deals? (9)

indicatorNotes.about: firm and sanctioned sit about, i.e. around, the member

annotation.surface: A company given official approval over an MP, amid hints of shady dealings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sanctioned' can mean penalised, which suits the dodgy deals, but here it means approved: LICIT.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: shady dealing is one kind of wrongdoing a complicit person takes part in, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Television also broadcast fight (3-2)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: spoken, so 'too' can stand for its sound-alike

annotation.surface: A TV network also airs a boxing match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the television, but it is the sound instruction on 'also'.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal British idiom: a set-to is a brief scrap or heated quarrel.

entries.clue: Overcomes unacceptable methods of Speaker (9)

indicatorNotes.of Speaker: words 'of a speaker' are heard rather than read, so the answer only sounds like the phrase

annotation.surface: Someone defeats the Speaker's improper procedures in the Commons.
annotation.walkthrough: The Speaker suggests the House of Commons, but it just means the words are spoken. 'Out' means not acceptable, as in 'that's out'.
annotation.definitionFit: To outweigh is to be greater than, to overcome.

entries.clue: Gave drugs to note first signs of side effects directly (5)

indicatorNotes.first signs of: take the first letter of each word
indicatorNotes.directly: the letters follow straight after the note

blocks.note: do, the first note of the sol-fa scale
first letters of side, effects, directly

annotation.surface: A doctor medicated a patient, noting the earliest side effects straight away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Directly' reads as an adverb for 'note', but its first letter is part of the answer too.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a dose is a measured amount of medicine, and the verb means administering it.

entries.clue: Benefit surrounding success mushrooms (7)

indicatorNotes.surrounding: the benefit goes round the success

blocks.note: for the sake of = for the benefit of; split S…AKE

annotation.surface: A charity event around a hit show, perhaps selling mushrooms.
annotation.walkthrough: This spelling, SHITAKE, is a less common variant of shiitake, the Japanese mushroom.
annotation.definitionFit: Shiitake, also spelt shitake, are Japanese edible mushrooms.
annotation.definitionNote: plural in the clue: shitake is used as a plural too

entries.clue: Childhood implies those cases presenting as most depressed superficially? (9)

indicatorNotes.cases presenting: the phrase holds the answer in its casing and presents it

annotation.surface: A pediatric study suggests which cases seem most seriously depressed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depressed' suggests mood, but the question mark signals the literal sense: a dimple is a small dent in the surface of the skin.
annotation.definitionFit: Dimpliest means having the most dimples, the most small hollows on the surface.

entries.clue: Opening of epic Gaelic novel written in verse form (7)

indicatorNotes.Opening of: a word opens with its first letter, so only the E of epic is taken
indicatorNotes.novel: novel means new, so Gaelic takes a new form

annotation.surface: The start of an epic Irish or Scots Gaelic novel written as poetry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' sits among books and verse as a noun, but it is the adjective 'new', an anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Elegiac describes verse written in elegiacs, the classical couplet form used for elegies.

entries.clue: Union member doing fine in correctional facility (9)

blocks.note: one member of a marriage union

annotation.surface: A trade union member is getting on fine in prison.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union; it is a marriage. Bridewell was a London prison, and the name became a general word for a jail.
annotation.definitionFit: A bridewell is a house of correction, a jail.

entries.clue: Flyers typically seen in night clubs (4)

blocks.note: clubs for hitting a ball, as in cricket or baseball

annotation.surface: Party animals usually spotted in nightclubs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Night clubs' reads as one place to go dancing; it splits into the end of the first definition and a second.
annotation.definitionFit: Bats fly at night, and bats are clubs used to hit a ball.

entries.clue: English nation turning strangely frightening (5)

annotation.surface: An English country growing oddly scary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' looks like an anagram indicator, but it belongs to the definition; the turning is a plain reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the whole phrase: eerie fear is the uncanny kind, frightening because it is strange.

entries.clue: Important piece of music that man encountered when cycling (5)

indicatorNotes.when cycling: the last letter moves round to the front

annotation.surface: A tune a man happened upon while out on his bike.
annotation.walkthrough: HEMET cycled, with its final T brought to the front, gives THEME.
annotation.definitionFit: A theme is the main melody a piece is built on, so its most important part.

entries.clue: What may be used to flog waste ground (5)

annotation.definition: What may be used to flog

indicatorNotes.ground: waste is ground up, broken down

annotation.surface: A whip for sale found on a patch of wasteland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Waste ground' is a phrase for derelict land; 'ground' is the anagram indicator. A tawse is a Scottish leather strap once used to punish schoolchildren. 'Flog' can mean sell as well as beat.
annotation.definitionFit: A tawse is a leather strap used for beating.

entries.clue: Advertisement reinvented retail therapy essentially (7)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence, the middle letter, of therapy

annotation.surface: An advert for a new take on shopping as a mood-lifter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retail therapy' is a set phrase for shopping to cheer up; the words split between anagram fodder and a middle letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A trailer is an advertisement for a forthcoming film or programme.

entries.clue: Threatening to incarcerate Liberal in protective housing (7)

indicatorNotes.to incarcerate: the threatening word locks up the L

annotation.surface: Politicians menacing to lock up a Liberal inside a secure building.
annotation.walkthrough: A cowling is the removable cover over an engine.
annotation.definitionFit: A cowling is a protective metal cover housing an engine.

entries.clue: Novel exploit restricted to most of these hosts (7,3,4)

indicatorNotes.most of: most of a word is all but a little, so its last letter is dropped
indicatorNotes.hosts: the shortened word takes the exploit inside

blocks.note: as in 'between ourselves' = restricted to us
THESE without its last E; split THE…S
an act = a deed, an exploit

annotation.surface: A new stunt only for most of the people hosting the event.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' reads as the adjective 'new' before exploit, but it is the definition: Virginia Woolf's last novel.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Virginia Woolf's final work, published in 1941, is a novel.
